key_insight: AI agents can improve fixed game policies through heuristic learning, but they still struggle to reach the top in more complex adversarial games.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a practical agent-centered workflow for iteratively refining game software under strict match and evaluation budgets without retraining model weights.
method: Define Adversarial Heuristic Learning (AHL): agents revise executable policies, not model weights.
Benchmark on AAArena with 12 adversarial games and 1,920 archived human programs.
Agents interpret rules, select opponents, analyze replays, and update game agents within competition-like constraints.
evidence_signal: Across evaluated configurations, Opus5.5 with Claude Code won 6 gold medals, but no configuration led the remaining 6 human ladders, with weaker results in games with more complex rules.
watch_item: Performance depends heavily on rule complexity and the quality of opponent selection/feedback, so results may not transfer cleanly to harder or less well-specified games.
paper_title: Can AI Agents Learn Their Way to the Top? Evaluating Heuristic Learning in a Long-Running Game Agent Competition
